label: Second copy step (recall_idx 1) of long sequences (L>=7), favoring certain first tokens
explanation: Fires almost only at step L+1, the first step after <DEL> where the input is the model fed-back orig(0) and the output is orig(1) (99.98% of activations; never in the original phase, at the delimiter, or at recall_idx >= 2). Rate rises steeply with L: 0 for L<=4, ~0.1% at L=6, 9% at L=9, so 99% of mass is at L>=7. Within that slot, firing is gated by token identity in a distributed way: the input/first token (h, 2, r strongest; then x, l, i, y, g, m, 0, o, 1), the output orig(1) (q, 1, p, x, y strongest) and the next output orig(2) (s, q, t, u, v, w) all raise the rate. Top activations (up to 4.3) are L=8-9 sequences starting with r/2/h/l followed by q or 1. The predicate (slot + L>=7 + first-token set) captures ~89% of mass but has precision ~0.35; adding out_tok/next_out sets raises dev F1 only to ~0.58, so the token dependence is a graded mix rather than a clean rule.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=9: h, 2, r, x; t=10: h, r, 2, x; t=8: h, r, 2, i) and the third original token (most: q, u, s, t, v, w; least: r, l, i, h); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=10, L=8 & t=9.
